correctness.rationale: Each positive best response to effort s is sqrt(s/a)−s in its interior region, giving F_c(y)=sqrt((sqrt y-y)/c)−(sqrt y-y), positive analytic near the stated equilibrium. F_c derivative at y*=−(c−1)²/(4c), crossing −1 at c*. The actual source verification/check.py uses rational pairs Q(sqrt2) to check full order-five Taylor coefficients and composition (degrees 2,3,4 vanish), coefficient K positive by exact reciprocal (99+70sqrt2)/512. The iterated normal form z→z−Kz^5+O(z^6) gives k^(1/4) z_k→signed(4K)^(-1/4) via telescoped inverse fourth powers. For δ>0, dividing the nontrivial fixed-point equation of F_c² by z gives alpha δ−Kz^4 plus controlled error, and analytic zero counting plus scaling identifies exactly 2 real and 2 nonreal nearby zeros. The real two are exchanged by F and attract with the stated multiplier; δ<0 has no nearby nonzero real period-two root. Independent high-precision derivatives and composition matched the quintic coefficient. Finite orbit samples only corroborate the analytic zero argument.
residual_risks: The result concerns locally positive best-response branches; zero-effort convention and global basins are out of scope.
The 1/4 exponent requires the exact all-order-five cancellation, not just numerical near −1 slopes.
